name: Veal rolled in rice paper
summary: The veal plate three publishers describe, and they do not cook it the same way. Người Lao Động and Tuổi Trẻ boil it and roll it with forest greens. Báo Quốc tế grills it just done and rolls it the same way.
origin: Củ Chi. Người Lao Động, Tuổi Trẻ on 25 Jun 2018, and Báo Quốc tế each describe bò tơ cuốn bánh tráng. Tuổi Trẻ calls the boiled roll the plate people order most.
howToEat: Người Lao Động: thin rounds with the skin, boiled or steamed with spring-onion tops and a little ginger. Roll bánh tráng phơi sương with forest greens, a little bún, and sour pickles. Dip in sweet-sour fish sauce, or in mắm nêm with chopped pineapple.

Tuổi Trẻ: boiled veal rolled with forest greens and rice paper. The greens named there are lá cóc, lá ổi, celery, spring onion, and mango tips. The same article also describes thinly sliced belly or shank rolled with raw greens in rice paper.
Báo Quốc tế: veal grilled just done, rolled in rice paper with forest greens and a dipping sauce. It does not name the sauce.
All three stay. No price was printed. Check on arrival. The hour is Check on arrival.
where: No street was printed. Check on arrival
seoTitle: Veal rolled in rice paper in Cu Chi
seoDescription: Cu Chi veal in rice paper with forest greens. Boiled on two accounts, grilled just done on Báo Quốc tế. The price is Check on arrival.
taste: Người Lao Động calls the boiled meat soft and fragrant. Tuổi Trẻ calls it soft and sweet, with crisp skin. Báo Quốc tế calls the meat soft and fragrant and describes it grilled just done.
